items.headline: Ukraine reportedly drone-strikes sanctioned Russian tanker Sparta II in the Baltic; vessel drifts into Finnish waters, NATO airspace tensions spill over
items.summary: The Sparta II, a Russian cargo ship under US sanctions bound for Kaliningrad, was struck by drones in international waters west of Gogland island late Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters; Finland called in Swedish combat aircraft and Estonian naval support, and all 16 crew were evacuated. It came a day after a Russian missile reportedly violated Polish airspace, underscoring a widening Baltic-NATO risk corridor beyond Ukraine's borders.
items.actionable: A genuine NATO-adjacent escalation (Finnish/Swedish/Estonian military assets scrambled for a sanctioned Russian vessel) rather than a Ukraine-only story -- raises tail risk of a Baltic shipping/insurance disruption that would be a fresh, independent bid for oil/gas alongside the Hormuz tanker attacks, worth monitoring for any SGX-listed shipping or energy-linked spillover.

items.headline: Two tankers hit by projectiles near Strait of Hormuz as Iran escalates shipping blockade; ~25 incidents in a week, Sunday oil futures reopen to price it in
items.summary: UK Maritime Trade Operations reported two tankers struck near Oman's Khasab on Saturday -- one hit in the stern, another in the engine room -- while Iran's navy separately claimed a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted zone; no casualties were reported. Al Jazeera's correspondent counted roughly 25 such incidents over the preceding week (about three daily) as Iran asserts all Hormuz passage must be coordinated with its navy, in apparent retaliation for a continuing US blockade of Iranian ports.
items.actionable: This is the concrete catalyst Sunday-evening oil futures will reopen against -- a genuine supply-side risk premium building in the world's most important chokepoint, distinct from Friday's AI-driven equity rout; worth tracking for a potential energy-sector hedge or re-rating opportunity even as the portfolio has no direct oil holding.

items.headline: Bitcoin crashes below $57,000 (two-year low $55,130) on a $2.4bn liquidation wave, then rebounds 9% to retake $60,300 as forced selling clears
items.summary: Coinglass data showed $2.4bn in crypto futures liquidated in 24 hours (over $1bn in BTC futures, $545m in ETH futures) as Bitcoin crashed to a two-year low near $55,130 and Ether dropped toward $1,560; Glassnode said the flush cleared a stale cluster of leveraged long bets between $59,000-$62,000 that had built up over months. Bitcoin then rebounded 9% to ~$60,300 by Saturday afternoon as that forced-selling pressure abated, though QCP Capital cautioned a durable recovery needs tech-equity stabilization and returning institutional ETF flows.
items.actionable: Confirms crypto's weekend round trip was leverage-flush-and-release mechanics layered on top of the existing multi-week ETF-outflow/MSCI-removal drain, not a new standalone shock -- the bounce off $55k is a useful reference level, but QCP's conditioning on equity stabilization means Monday's Asia open (and any Nvidia/Broadcom follow-through) is the key swing factor for whether $60k holds.

items.headline: Nvidia's seven-week losing streak (-46%, worst since 2008) now compounds an SEC accounting probe, a California AG subpoena, and a CEO exit -- weekend press digests the pile-up
items.summary: Weekend coverage (24/7 Wall St, Yahoo Finance) framed Nvidia's slide as its longest weekly losing streak since 2008, down 46% over seven weeks and roughly $2.6tn in market value, even as the company's revenue run-rate dwarfs 2008 levels. The pile-up now includes Friday's Reuters-reported SEC accounting probe, a Nov 19 California AG subpoena probing whether ex-CEO Jensen Huang's personal ties to China led to chip/secrets diversion or misleading disclosures, and interim-CEO transition to CFO Colette Kress after Huang's Nov 12 resignation.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but this is now a multi-pronged credibility crisis (SEC + state AG + governance vacuum), not a one-headline shock, which raises the odds of continued AI-capex-narrative contagion into HK tech's own buildout story (0700.HK, 0981.HK) at Monday's Asia open rather than a one-day bounce-back.

items.headline: Needham reinstates MP Materials at Buy with a $48/share target as three insiders put $3.6m into shares near the 52-week low
items.summary: Needham resumed coverage of MP Materials with a Buy rating and a $48/share price target, arguing the company is in the early innings of a transformation from miner to vertically integrated rare-earth/magnet supplier, with commercial magnet deliveries to GM expected in Q4 2026 and Apple-linked magnet revenue flagged for H2 2027. Separately, three MP Materials insiders bought a combined $3.6m of stock between Nov 10-17 near the 52-week low, even as the broader rare-earth complex (Critical Metals -8%, USAR -5%) extended its Nov 20 selloff.
items.actionable: Insider buying plus a fresh sell-side reinstatement at a meaningful premium to spot is a genuine fundamental counter-signal for the owner's MP position sitting inside a broader rare-earth group that just got hit by Friday's macro-driven reversal -- worth distinguishing this company-specific bull case from the sector-wide feedstock-delay bear case already flagged on USAR.

items.headline: Gold holds near 14-month low around $3,500-3,538, silver near $41, as weekend commentary splits between 'margin-call capitulation' and 'genuine bear market' reads
items.summary: Spot gold traded around $3,502-3,538/oz over the weekend -- down more than 30% from January's all-time high and its lowest since September 2025 -- while silver held near $41/oz. Kitco's weekend roundup (citing Rich Checkan and others) argued the move is margin-call-driven forced liquidation rather than owners of physical metal exiting, while rising Treasury yields, a firmer dollar, and swelling December-hike bets continue to work against both metals into Monday's Asia open.
items.actionable: Weekend commentary has not resolved the margin-call-vs-bear-market debate that matters most for the owner's leveraged silver/miners book -- gold/silver holding steady rather than extending Friday's rout over the weekend is a mild positive sign for a Monday bounce, but the real-rate/dollar/hike-odds backdrop remains unambiguously hostile.

items.headline: CME FedWatch odds of a December 25bp hike surge to ~97%, up from 76% a month ago, after Waller floats a 50bp 'shock' move
items.summary: Futures markets now assign roughly 96.9% probability to a quarter-point Fed hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC (vs 76.3% a month earlier), with hold odds down to about 3% and a 50bp move still a tail outcome; the repricing follows Governor Waller's comments that the Fed may need to shock inflation expectations lower given stubborn ~3% inflation.
items.actionable: A near-certain December hike is now priced, not just debated -- this is the macro backdrop both the owner's SGX bank/REIT exposure (financing costs) and levered silver/miners position (real-rate/dollar channel) must absorb into year-end regardless of how the Nvidia/crypto/oil stories resolve.

items.headline: California AG Bonta subpoenas Nvidia over Jensen Huang's alleged ties to a Chinese national, probing chip/secrets diversion and investor disclosures
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia following reports that former CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to have intelligence ties, alongside two relationships with Nvidia employees. Bonta's office is investigating whether the relationship enabled China to obtain Nvidia's advanced chips or confidential information, and whether the company's public disclosures misled investors -- running in parallel with Congress's own move to subpoena Huang and the SEC's accounting probe.
items.actionable: A third, independent legal front (state AG, beyond the SEC and DOJ) targeting the same company whose chip-export-control stance already weighs on Tencent's AI roadmap (0700.HK) -- raises the odds that US-China tech decoupling rhetoric intensifies further, a tail risk worth monitoring for the HK tech book even without direct NVDA exposure.

items.headline: US and Venezuela sign military partnership agreement in Caracas, first since January's Maduro extraction
items.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited Caracas and signed a military cooperation agreement with Venezuela's interim government (Acting President Delcy Rodriguez), covering joint training, intelligence sharing, and border security, framed around counter-narcotics operations. It is the first formal US-Venezuela military tie-up since US special forces extracted then-President Maduro in a January raid.
items.actionable: A genuine US-Venezuela thaw that could eventually affect regional oil supply dynamics, though it is a slower-moving structural story rather than a weekend price driver -- lower priority than the Hormuz/Baltic escalations for immediate portfolio relevance, flagged mainly as background context for the energy/geopolitics picture.

items.headline: Russia launches ~150-drone, 3-missile overnight barrage on Ukraine, killing a 7-year-old and a paramedic in Kryvyi Rih
items.summary: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched three ballistic missiles and 148 drones (87 jet-powered) overnight into Saturday, with strikes on Kryvyi Rih killing a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic and a drone strike on a Kharkiv-region residential building injuring 11, including two children. The barrage came one day after a Russian missile reportedly violated Polish airspace and the same weekend Ukraine allegedly struck a sanctioned Russian tanker in the Baltic, underscoring the conflict's continued intensity despite the Shenzhen trilateral's de-escalatory rhetoric.
items.actionable: Confirms the Russia-Ukraine track is escalating, not cooling, in parallel with (not instead of) the Trump-Xi-Putin summit optics -- relevant tail risk for safe-haven flows (gold/silver, already saturated by margin selling) and worth tracking for any NATO-direct-involvement escalation that would shift the macro narrative away from pure AI-capex jitters.
